clue.text: To fix a fight can result in attack

parts.note: to fix something in place is to set it
a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: Rigging a boxing match may provoke an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To set about someone is an idiom for launching an assault on them.

clue.text: Trying to make notes about a politician on the Left

indicators.note: about means around, so the words for singing go around the rest

parts.note: to make musical notes is to sing
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A struggle to take notes concerning a left-wing politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food is tasting it, trying it out.

clue.text: Order relates to bears

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command concerning grizzlies.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it, endure it.

clue.text: Went to pieces, having no resources

explanation.surface: Someone fell apart after losing all their money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that shattered has fallen apart; someone penniless is skint, without funds.

clue.text: £1 invested in battered suite that's put to good use

indicators.note: money invested in something is placed inside it
a battered suite is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pound
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Spending a pound on a worn-out sofa set to make it useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges SUITE into UTISE; 'invested in' puts LI inside it, after UTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something for a practical purpose is to make use of it.

clue.text: The doctor too may be a cowboy!

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
too, as in 'too much', means over, as in 'overmuch'

explanation.surface: A doctor might also turn out to be a cattle rancher out West.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover herds livestock over long distances, the work of a cattle hand.

clue.text: Remember to note the day's prayer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a collect is the short prayer set for a given day in church services

explanation.surface: A reminder to jot down today's prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: An instrument for playing in the garden?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a musical instrument may be played outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin, and also a pansy-like flower grown in beds.

clue.text: Bacon could be more audacious

explanation.surface: Speculating that Francis Bacon might have been bolder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon is called by this name; it also means more reckless, comparative of hasty.

clue.text: American song-writer's nurse

explanation.surface: The carer belonging to an American tunesmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Foster wrote 'Oh! Susanna'; to foster is to nurture or rear a child.

clue.text: Very musical

parts.note: read as 'the musical term for very', the Italian direction a score uses to intensify a marking

explanation.surface: Someone extremely fond of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian direction on a score asks for an effect to be strengthened, as in 'much' or 'very' allegro.

clue.text: Smooth foil used for decoration

parts.note: to smooth clothes is to iron them
to foil a plan is to thwart or cross it

explanation.surface: A flat piece of metal foil employed as an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Cross is a German military medal, so 'decoration' here means an award for bravery rather than an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A military medal is a decoration, an honour pinned on a uniform.

clue.text: The burglar, it's clear, isn't disturbed

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of their order, so these words get rearranged

explanation.surface: A housebreaker is plainly unruffled by his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges CLEAR and ISNT; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits theft, and a burglar is a thief who breaks into buildings.

clue.text: Don't eat in desert

explanation.surface: Advice to fast while out in the wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a plate untouched is not to eat it; to abandon a person or post is to desert.

clue.text: Lack of food is rare

parts.note: no, as in 'no money', expresses a lack
table can mean the food served, as in 'she keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: Going hungry is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable and worth noting is uncommon, so rare in that sense.

clue.text: Warder organising a fete getting in the drink

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the rearranged letters go inside the drink

parts.note: beer is the drink, as in a pub

indicators.note: organising puts things in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A prison guard running a summer fair takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' makes EFEAT from A FETE, which 'getting in' places inside BEER after BE. Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders guarding the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London go by this nickname.

clue.text: Cigarette in jacket

explanation.surface: A smoke tucked into a coat pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a cannabis joint and also names a short double-breasted sailor's coat.

clue.text: Curses when running ' water packs up

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, flowing water
to crate goods is to pack them in boxes

explanation.surface: Someone swears when the plumbing fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs up' looks like a breakdown, but it is boxing goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or damn.

clue.text: Sort of clothing that makes fellows curse

parts.note: fellows are men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Garments that make the men who wear them swear.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments designed for males make up this category of attire.

clue.text: Approve a head's retirement before the end of August

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for head is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

indicators.note: the end of August is its final letter

explanation.surface: A headmaster's leaving is agreed ahead of late August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns NESS into SSEN; the 's of head's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give assent is to agree to or sanction something.

clue.text: The gift of a story book

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A present of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is often called a gift.

clue.text: Catch sight of animal in street light

parts.note: 'of animal' is read as a possessive, a cat's
to catch sight of something is to eye it

explanation.surface: Spotting a creature in the glow of a lamp-post.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-eye is a glass reflector set in the road surface that shines in headlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflective studs marking road lanes act as lights for night drivers.

clue.text: Willing to discover what is inside

explanation.surface: Happy to find out what something holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied and agreeable is a sense of the adjective; the stressed-first noun means what a container holds.

clue.text: Man cutting a fine figure in uniform

definitions.text: Man cutting a fine figure in uniform

parts.words: Man cutting a fine figure in uniform
parts.note: read as a smart soldier, but 'cutting' hints at a man who pierces with a long spear

explanation.surface: A dashing fellow in military dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalryman armed with a lance cut a dashing figure in his regimental uniform.

clue.text: Extensive map redrawn by the French

indicators.note: a map redrawn has its lines laid out afresh, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A large-scale map revised by French cartographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrawn' turns MAP into AMP, and 'by' simply joins it to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or wide-ranging.

clue.text: Policeman keeping up in a state of terror.

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the policeman's letters hold the others

parts.note: PC is a police constable

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An officer staying alert amid widespread fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IN A into ANI, which 'keeping' places inside PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear is a state of alarm.

clue.text: Guides left with foreign coins.

parts.note: with means together with, and
the mark was the German currency

explanation.surface: Tour guides were left holding foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent features that help travellers find their way serve as guides.

clue.text: Note there's just a drop

explanation.surface: Remarking there's only a tiny bit left.
explanation.definitionFit: A half note in music bears this name, and it is also a tiny apothecaries' measure of liquid, a drop.

clue.text: A woman's standing after study

indicators.note: after puts the word for standing behind the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a stance is a way of standing

explanation.surface: A woman's social position follows her education.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a female first name; its 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, meaning steadfastness.

clue.text: Some cooks use it to season — it replaces salt

indicators.note: some here means a portion of the following words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: some cooks season with this as a substitute for salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks letters spanning 'season — it replaces'. The surface rings true: this salt (saltpetre) is used in curing meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, saltpetre, is a chemical salt.

clue.text: A minute log

explanation.surface: A very small tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes of a meeting are its written account, as is a ship's log.

clue.text: This can split up, but it's more a compound

indicators.note: to compound is to mix ingredients together, so these words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemistry remark: a compound breaks apart more readily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a noun, but it is the anagram signal for ITSMOREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent spray breaks liquid into a fine mist of droplets.
